title: uuencoding::encode mode parameter: behavior for values > 0o777 undocumented
description: uuencoding::encode() takes a mode: u32 parameter that represents the Unix file permission bits in octal. The UU format uses 6 bits (0o77) per encoded character, and the standard begin line writes the mode as 3 octal digits (0-0o777). What happens when a caller passes 0o1777 (setuid/sticky bit) or 0xFFFFFFFF is not documented. What goes wrong: callers producing UU archives for interoperability with other decoders will silently truncate the mode if the implementation masks it, or produce non-standard output if it doesn't. The fix is to document exactly which bits are preserved and what happens to values outside 0o000–0o777, or to accept a newtype (e.g. UnixMode(u16)) that encodes the constraint. File: uuencoding/src/lib.rs.
close_reason: Already documented in this session's changes — mode is formatted as {:03o} and the doc comment explicitly states values above 0o7777 produce longer mode strings. Test encode_mode_large_value covers u32::MAX.
